newsitem.title: UK: Euro Products Outlook - Mostly flat, gas oil holds.
newsitem.headline: Euro Products Outlook - Mostly flat, gas oil holds.

text.p: European oil products are set to stay mostly flat this week but some areas of the barrel like gas oil are holding firm, traders said.
Gasoline is likely to stay broadly stable this week with barges are well supplied but cargoes are tight after sales last week into Germany and the Unitied States.
More than 100,000 tonnes of gasoline was sold to U.S. buyers in recent days with cargoes loading up to the middle of August.
But demand into Germany has been covered and many dealers believe only the U.S. can lend further support.

August NYMEX mogas look set to remain firm due to tightness on octane boosters on the east coast. High octane grades in Europe are tight due to lower than normal supplies from Neste and Dreyfus while low octane is in steady demand from Nigeria.
Naphtha is also well supported and could make gains this week after bucking the weaker tone in recent days.
Dealers said they expected some tightness for prompt loadings and saw good demand from Asia keeping August swaps at or above $180 a tonne.
European gas oil prices are expected to hold firm with tight ARA supplies underpinning barge and cargo premiums.
Supplies were not heavily swelled last week by a delivery from the expiring July gas oil futures contract of 122,300 tonnes.
"The delivery was easily absorbed without spooking the market and Germany needs to buy more product," one broker said.
Traders said the only downside could be if additional cargoes start to move up from the Mediterranean, though supplies of most grades are tight there too.
In the Mediterranean diesel could continue to strengthen as supplies tighten with refiners reluctant to run the more expensive EN590 due to its narrow premium to heating oil.
"Refiners are reluctant to run EN590 while the differential to 0.2 sulphur material is so small" one trader said.
However, a weaker Far East market will limit arbitrage opportunities for any surplus that does occur though traders said some product could find it's way North if the NWE market does continue firm.
"It works to the North but cargo avails are limited at the moment though some Russians are coming soon," on trader said.
High sulphur fuel oil cargoes are expected to remain steady, with sellers asking $84 to $85 cif Rotterdam at least at the start of the week.
But, with more Russian cargoes coming in soon, some downward pressure was expected later.
Scarcer straight-run Russian material is set to continue. Offers have risen to as high at $5 or $6 over two means last week.
"As long as crude margins continue to be bad there will be demand for straight-run," one trader said.
Low sulphur cargoes should continue in the $92 to $94 fob range this week, traders said.
